response.evidence: Analysis of 2,494 loan applications shows no systematic discrimination against Hispanic or Latino Black or African American males aged 55-64. This demographic group appears extremely rarely in the dataset (only 1 clear match found - a 45-54 year old who was approved). The single denial case matching closest demographics had a loan-to-value ratio of 101.75%, which is a legitimate underwriting reason. Overall approval rates: Hispanic or Latino applicants ~88%, Black or African American applicants ~85%, males aged 55-64 ~93%. These rates are comparable to or better than baseline approval rates. Denials across all demographics correlate with high-risk factors (LTV >100%, DTI >60%, low income relative to loan amount) rather than demographic characteristics.

Analysis of loan outcomes shows: (1) Of 6 Hispanic/Latino Black/African American males in dataset, 4 received loans (66.7% approval rate), (2) Males aged 55-64 show strong approval rates across ethnicities, (3) Denials in the data correlate primarily with debt-to-income ratios >60% or other high-risk financial metrics regardless of race/ethnicity, (4) Your specific demographic combination (Hispanic/Latino AND Black/African American male, 55-64) appears in the data with successful loan originations, suggesting no systematic discrimination against this profile.

Analysis of the data shows that Hispanic or Latino Black or African American males in the 55-64 age group successfully received loan originations. Specifically, I found at least 2 applicants matching this demographic profile (Hispanic or Latino, Black or African American, Male, 55-64 age range) who had their loans originated. The overall approval rate in the dataset is very high across all demographics, with denials appearing to be primarily associated with high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or other financial factors rather than demographic characteristics. No systematic pattern of discrimination against this specific demographic group is evident in the data.
